script.explain:
Lua scripts. on_receive runs after data arrives; before_send intercepts every outgoing frame (including quick commands, batch and auto reply) and sends what it returns, or nothing if it returns nil.
Click a row to open the editor and run log below the data log; the log and send box stay visible. The switch only controls automatic runs; Run tries the script once at any time.
Not sure how to write one? Open Tutorial: six lessons from reading frames to adding a CRC.
script.tutorialNote:
Indexes start at 1; 0x literals work as usual; infinite loops are aborted automatically and dangerous functions such as os.execute are removed.
Try sample feeds this lesson's sample frame to the code and writes the output to the run log; nothing is sent.

hooks.title: When scripts run
hooks.brief: Two hooks: after receiving, before sending
hooks.text: Define a function named on_receive and it is called for every packet received; frame holds that packet's bytes. Define before_send and it is called before every outgoing frame (send button, quick commands, batch and auto reply), and only the frame it returns is sent. The switch only controls automatic runs; Run dry-runs with the last received frame or the send box, and never sends.

print.title: Print a frame
print.brief: log writes to the run log; frames show as HEX
print.text: log writes to the run log, joining arguments with spaces; print is the same function. A frame passed directly shows as HEX, frame:sub(i, j) takes bytes i to j, and frame:str() turns it into ASCII text.

parse.title: Match a header, read values
parse.brief: starts_with checks the header, u16 reads two bytes
parse.text: frame:starts_with(0xA5, 0x5A, 0x03) checks the header; return early for frames you don't want. Indexes start at 1: u8(i) reads byte i, u16(i) combines bytes i and i+1 big-endian, and u16le(i) reads little-endian.

checksum.title: Add a checksum before sending
checksum.brief: before_send returns the changed frame; append adds bytes
checksum.text: before_send receives the frame about to go out and sends whatever it returns. frame:append(...) returns a new frame with bytes added at the end; sum8 is the additive sum and xor8 is XOR (BCC).

block.title: Block frames you don't want sent
block.brief: Return nil and the frame is not sent
block.text: When before_send returns nil the frame is not sent and the data log records the block. Pass every other frame through with return frame.

modbus.title: Modbus CRC16
modbus.brief: crc16 returns the low byte, then the high byte
modbus.text: crc16(frame) uses the Modbus algorithm and returns two values, low byte then high byte, which is the order Modbus RTU appends them. frame(...) builds a new frame from numbers, strings or other frames.

reply.explain: When received data matches, replies are sent in order. Each delay starts after the previous reply.
reply.name: Name
reply.hintTemplateHex: ?? matches any one byte, * matches any length; use \$1, \$2 in replies for the bytes they matched
reply.hintTemplateAscii: ? matches any one byte, * any length; \\? \\* \\r \\n \\xHH are literals; use \$1, \$2 in replies
reply.hintRegexHex: Matched against spaced uppercase HEX (e.g. A5 5A 03); write ^ and \$ yourself; use \$1, \$2 for groups
reply.hintRegexAscii: Matched against the raw bytes; write ^ and \$ yourself; use \$1, \$2 for groups
reply.tutorNote: Four template lessons, three regex lessons. Open one to fill the form.
reply.tutorWrote: Written on the left. Save to add it to the rule list.

order.title: Nothing is sent until a packet arrives
order.brief: Replies go out in list order
order.name: Handshake reply
order.text: While the port is open, every received packet is compared with each enabled rule. A hit sends the reply list in order. Each delay starts after the previous reply, not from the moment the packet arrived. Two matching rules both reply. Nothing runs while the port is closed.
order.rxNote: Prefix only looks at the leading A5 5A. The last two bytes are not compared.

place.title: Prefix, full frame, contains, suffix
place.name: Reply when it appears
place.text: The same pattern A5 5A hits or misses depending on where you look. Full frame must be exactly those bytes. Prefix checks the start, suffix the end, contains anywhere in the middle. Regex has no such menu: write ^ and \$ yourself.
place.rxNote: This packet starts with 00. Prefix misses; contains hits.

wild.title: ?? takes one byte, * takes a span
wild.brief: Wildcards become \$1, \$2 from left to right
wild.name: Echo captured bytes
wild.text: In a HEX template, ?? is any one byte and must be written as two question marks; a single ? will not save. * is any length, including empty. They become \$1 and \$2 from left to right, and writing \$1 in a reply substitutes the captured bytes. Templates are checked on save: \$3 is rejected when there is no third wildcard.
wild.rxNote: Full frame. ?? takes 11, * takes the remaining 22 33.

ascii.title: In ASCII, one ? is one byte
ascii.brief: The reply box is still HEX
ascii.name: Echo the byte after OK
ascii.text: With ASCII, one ? is any single byte and * is still any length. To match a question mark itself, write a backslash before it; the same for star, carriage return and line feed. A specific byte is backslash, x, and two hex digits, for example \\x0D. Ignore case exists only for ASCII. Replies are always HEX: the character 7 comes back as byte 37.
ascii.rxNote: Ignore case is on, so ok,7 matches OK,?. The question mark captures the character 7.

reword.title: Regex sees a line of HEX text
reword.brief: * here does not mean any length
reword.name: Byte after the header
reword.text: Choosing regex removes the match menu. A HEX regex is not compared byte by byte; it is compared with the spaced hex text, such as A5 5A 03. * means “repeat the previous item”, and ?? is not “any one byte”. To capture one byte, wrap two hex digits: ([0-9A-F]{2}). Write ^ and \$ yourself.
reword.rxNote: The engine matches the text “A5 5A 03”. Without \$, extra bytes afterward still hit.

groups.title: Only parentheses become \$1
groups.name: Split two bytes
groups.text: A template’s ?? and * are numbered automatically. In a regex only parentheses become \$1 and \$2, in the order the opening parentheses appear. This lesson anchors the whole frame with \$. If a reply uses \$3 but there are only two groups, that reply is not sent and the log says the capture is missing. A group that catches only one hex digit is skipped the same way. A template would have blocked this at save time.
groups.rxNote: Two groups, \$1 then \$2. The final \$ means the frame ends there.

reascii.title: ASCII regex matches characters
reascii.brief: Compared as text, not as HEX words
reascii.name: After the comma
reascii.text: An ASCII regex walks the received characters, not the spaced hex text. Characters caught by parentheses are filled into the reply as bytes. Ignore case is available only for ASCII. Anchors are still ^ and \$, written by you.
reascii.rxNote: The characters are OK,42. (.+) puts both characters into the same \$1.

calc.explain: CRC16 is MODBUS (low byte first). CRC32 is IEEE (big-endian). Append writes the checksum into the send box.

dialog.deleteQuick: Delete quick command "$name"? This cannot be undone.
dialog.deleteFolder: Delete folder "$name"? This cannot be undone.
dialog.deleteFolderWith: Delete folder "$name" and the $count commands in it? This cannot be undone.
dialog.deleteRule: Delete rule "$name"? This cannot be undone.
dialog.deleteBatch: Delete batch "$name"? This cannot be undone.
dialog.deleteHistory: Delete all $count history entries? This cannot be undone.
dialog.deleteScript: Delete script "$name"? This cannot be undone.
dialog.aboutBody: Device Debug Tools · serial console. Open a port to send and receive.
dialog.aboutDetail: Quick commands, batch send, and auto-reply do nothing while the port is closed. Incoming bytes are merged by the packet timeout. Checksums: SUM8, XOR/BCC, LRC, CRC8, CRC16 (MODBUS, low byte first), CRC32 (IEEE, big-endian).
dialog.keySend: Send (while the send box is focused)
dialog.keyQuick: Send the quick command bound to that key
dialog.keyStop: Stop repeat send and batch send
dialog.fileRaw: Any file type works (.bin, .dat, .txt, …). The file's raw bytes are sent as-is, with no encoding conversion.
dialog.fileText: Hex characters in a text file are not parsed: a .txt containing "01 02" sends the ASCII codes of those 5 characters. Use a binary file to send HEX data.
dialog.fileAppend: If "Append checksum" or "Append CR LF" is checked, it is added after the file data. Escape parsing and AT auto-CR do not apply to files.
dialog.fileWhole: The whole file is read into memory and written in one go, without splitting. Split large files yourself to avoid UI stalls while sending.
dialog.filePreview: While a file is loaded the send box is read-only and previews only the first $count bytes. Click "Remove" or the send box's "Clear" to leave file mode.
dialog.fileLoop: With "Repeat every" checked, the whole file is resent on each period.
